title: Does the reduction split when the index halves (frozen side check)
claim: Run as frozen 2026-11-10 (pre-registered in f8e8b996c, sub-goal B91's first step): at the 61 eigenvalues with even k = 2c >= 4 for sides 16, 32 and 64, the reduction of the family to ker X_b (G monic) with the monomial complement or with the complement containing k G Y^j, in the parameter l of Zhat or u of Z(a + au)/(1 + u), has a nonzero entry with i + j odd below order 2k at every eigenvalue in every variant (S1 fails everywhere), so B91's strong form (the reduction at k = 2c splits into the parameter times the reductions at c and c - 1 with the parameter squared) is refuted at these sides; S2 (only odd powers on the parity-diagonal entries) holds at 33 of 61 eigenvalues for the monomial complement in u. The halving of the leading matrix (CHAIN-ORDERS-20261110-001A, Theorem 3) stands.
failure_conditions: Some variant passes S1 and S2 at every tested eigenvalue (then B91's strong form stands at these sides), or every variant fails somewhere (then it is refuted at these sides).
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10 (sub-goals B73 and B91).
